content: Clioquinol is a topical medication prescribed to treat various skin infections, including eczema, athlete's foot, jock itch, and ringworm. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other conditions, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Clioquinol is available in the form of a cream, lotion, or ointment, and it is applied directly to the skin. Typically, it is used two to four times daily for a duration of four weeks, except in the case of jock itch, where it is used for two weeks. Follow the instructions on the product label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed. Do not apply more or less than prescribed, and do not use it more frequently than recommended. Before application, thoroughly clean the affected area, allow it to dry, and then gently rub the medication into the skin until most of it is absorbed. Use only enough medication to cover the affected area. After applying the medication, wash your hands thoroughly. Before using clioquinol, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to clioquinol or any other medications. Additionally, provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription drugs, including vitamins, that you are currently taking. Notify your doctor if you are scheduled to undergo a thyroid function test, as clioquinol may interfere with the results. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using clioquinol, contact your doctor immediately. If you forget to apply a dose, do so as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Clioquinol may cause side effects. If you experience itching, burning, irritation, stinging, redness, or swelling, contact your doctor immediately. If you experience a severe side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store clioquinol in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Do not freeze the medication, and protect it from light. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor while using clioquinol. This medication is for external use only and may stain clothing, hair, skin, and nails yellow. Avoid contact with your eyes or mouth, and do not swallow the medication. Do not apply cosmetics, lotions, or other skin products to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If your symptoms persist after completing the course of clioquinol, contact your doctor.
